reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes Cr-V precipitate formation and radiation resistance in the baseline alloy but provides no data on Hf doping, its segregation behavior, or its effect on Cr/V mobility. The key premises about Hf's role are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Hf doping will segregate to grain boundaries and defect sinks in W38Ta36Cr15V11
Hf segregation will reduce Cr and V mobility and clustering tendency
Reduced Cr/V mobility will suppress Cr-V-rich precipitate formation at ~8 dpa
Suppressing precipitates will preserve low irradiation hardening and radiation resistance
Low Hf addition (~3 at.%) will not impair bulk manufacturability
